findings.title: `include_website_name` is missing `?` and `website_name` bypasses `untrusted_attributes` restrictions
findings.body:
`ActiveModel::Serializer` requires conditional inclusion methods to end with a question mark (`include_website_name?`). Because the method is defined as `def include_website_name`, it is never called by the serializer, causing `:website_name` to always be serialized in the JSON output (even as `nil` when the user has no website).

Additionally, `:website` is declared under `untrusted_attributes` (lines 105-111) so that it is hidden when an anonymous visitor views a TL0 user (`scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`). Because `:website_name` is not listed in `untrusted_attributes`, a TL0 user's website domain/path is still serialized and displayed on their profile (`{{#if model.website_name}}` in `user.hbs`) to anonymous users. Adding `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` (and removing the manual `include_website_name` method) will automatically define `include_website_name?` with both the `restrict_user_fields?` check and the `.present?` check.
